summary: Challis NF lookout made a station in 1913; present R-6 cab on a 10-foot concrete base dates to 1964; Chamber says no longer staffed, summit road open seasonally; registered 2014.

staffing.status: no longer staffed per Challis Chamber of Commerce; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as Drive-Up Staffed

access.note: Summit road usually open to vehicles late spring through fall, depending on snow (Challis Chamber). Sources do not describe public entry into the cab itself.

visit.trail_note: From Challis, turn onto Challis Creek Road and follow it about 20 miles to the summit, following signs. Last stretch may be rough or narrow; high-clearance vehicle recommended (Challis Chamber).

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Challis National Forest (listed as Salmon-Challis National Forest on current Forest Service pages)

events.note: Summit made a lookout station; a forest guard stationed there during the fire season (clipping dated September 6, 1913).
Alidade on the summit, with a log cabin about half a mile away.
7 x 7 lookout cabin of lumber packed to the site and native rock.
July 4, 1924: lightning struck guard V. E. Elliott on duty; he was knocked unconscious, and the strike badly damaged the roof and walls of the lookout building (clipping dated July 8, 1924).
L-4 cab per NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com. The Forest Lookouts page instead gives an R-1 14x14 live-in house replacing the older day-use building. See resolved_conflicts.

Present R-6 cab on a 10-foot concrete base, built to replace the 1932 lookout. A March 1965 clipping describes a two-story building with a cinder-block lower level, which the other sources do not mention.
Denver R James listed as staff (Former Forest Fire Lookout Registry).
Mike McCarty listed as staff (Former Forest Fire Lookout Registry).
Mark Cummins listed as staff for 1984 to 1985, the last staffing period on the Idaho Fire Lookouts list.
Registered March 14, 2014 as NHLR US 1002, ID 103.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com say a 1932 L-4 cab. The Forest Lookouts page reprints a 1932 entry for an R-1 14x14 live-in house replacing a day-use building. The story reports both.

NHLR, Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com describe an R-6 on a 10-foot concrete base. The March 1965 clipping describes a two-story building with a cinder-block lower level and a wooden upper floor.
NHLR gives 10,337 ft (3,151 m), which matches the brief's 3150.7 m. Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give 10,394 ft (about 3,168 m).

Challis Chamber says no longer staffed. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists it as Drive-Up Staffed. Firelookout.com calls it the highest active fire lookout. The Forest Service names three staffed lookouts, Long Tom, Middle Fork and Stein. The story reports the Chamber's statement and notes the conflict.

notes_for_editor: Three conflicts need an editor's call: the 1932 structure (L-4 vs R-1), the 1964 base (concrete vs cinder-block), and elevation (10,337 vs 10,394 ft). Current staffing is contested. Access is set to public on the Chamber's visitor listing; the cab's interior is not described, so confirm with Salmon-Challis NF before treating the cab as open. The brief's height_m of 3.0 is the base height, not total height. No rental found. The FS page names three staffed lookouts and does not name Twin Peaks, but it does not say which unstaffed lookouts remain.
